problem: REVERIE gives only a short, high-level instruction naming a remote target object, with no step-by-step route. VLN agents built for strict instruction-following do not exploit the room-type and object-type cues, or their commonsense relations, that are needed for goal-oriented exploration toward an unseen object.
motivation: Unlike R2R-style VLN, REVERIE success depends on reasoning about where a referred object is likely to be, for example which rooms contain which objects. The agent also has to remember what it has already seen while exploring. The paper's premise is that explicitly perceiving room and object entities in both language and vision, and linking them with commonsense knowledge, should guide exploration better than following the instruction alone.
key_idea: A transformer-based Cross-modality Knowledge Reasoning (CKR) agent keeps scene-memory tokens, attends separately to room- and object-type information in the instruction and in observations (ROAA), and reasons over commonsense-knowledge-based relations among room and object entities (KERR) to choose actions at each viewpoint.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so the ablations cannot be checked. The claim is that explicit room/object-aware attention plus commonsense entity-relationship reasoning yields large gains on REVERIE: a reported relative increase of 64.67% in SPL and 46.05% in REVERIE success rate. The implied lesson is that goal-oriented exploration benefits from structured semantic priors about room-object co-occurrence and from a memory of the explored scene, rather than from sequential instruction grounding alone.
method: Transformer-based CKR model: a cross-modal transformer policy that generates scene memory tokens summarizing history and uses them as clues for exploration.
Room-and-Object Aware Attention (ROAA): explicitly extracts room-type and object-type information from both the instruction and the visual observations via separate attention.

Knowledge-enabled Entity Relationship Reasoning (KERR): brings in external commonsense knowledge to learn internal-external correlations among room and object entities, used to score candidate actions at each viewpoint.
Action prediction on the REVERIE navigation graph, followed by localisation of the referred remote object (details not given in the abstract).

setting.backbone: Transformer-based CKR model with ROAA and KERR modules (trained; exact visual/language encoders not stated in abstract)
setting.training_data: REVERIE training split plus an external commonsense knowledge source (scale and specific knowledge base not stated in abstract)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views with object-level information (details not stated in abstract)

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract reports only relative improvements (SPL +64.67%, REVERIE success rate +46.05%), not absolute metric values
results: On the REVERIE benchmark, CKR reportedly raises SPL by 64.67% and REVERIE success rate (RGS) by 46.05%, both relative improvements over prior methods. The abstract does not give absolute numbers or name the baseline these gains are measured against.
limitations: Relies on an external commonsense knowledge source and explicit room/object categories, which may not transfer to open-vocabulary or unseen categories.
Only evaluated on REVERIE (per abstract); generalization to other goal-oriented navigation tasks is not shown.
